uncited: Marching Tetrahedra and Decomposition resolves the topological ambiguities inherent in standard Marching Cubes by decomposing each cubic voxel into a fixed set of tetrahedra, as implemented in [Marching Cubes Tetrahedron Decomposition](9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md).

It sets itself apart from [Subgrid Marching Tetrahedra](1737-subgrid-marching-tetrahedra.md) by operating on the primary voxel grid without sub-voxel refinement, and from [Error Analysis via Marching Tetrahedra](1308-error-analysis-via-marching-tetrahedra.md) by focusing on the geometric decomposition strategy itself rather than error metrics or topological fusion bounds.
For detailed traversal, surface determination, and mesh coherence mechanisms, see [Surface extraction](29-surface-extraction.md).
The specific origin (authors, date, paper) is Not given in the sources.

The method resolves the topological ambiguities present in the original Marching Cubes algorithm, which could produce non-manifold geometries in specific ambiguous cases [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md].
By decomposing the cube into tetrahedra, the problem is reduced to the 16 unambiguous cases of a tetrahedron [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md].
It is widely used in medical imaging and scientific visualization where topological correctness is critical [9029-marching-cubes-tetrahedron-decomposition.md].
